ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.69 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted off-route segment F3; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI ride, so distance actually driven enters the fare directly: F6 bills 13.19 km / $18.60 distance and $0.00 waiting, with no surge [F5] and only published add-ons (platform $1.47) [F6][RD-2]. The system record shows exactly one off-route segment, F3 (22:58–23:05, 3.82 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.91 km, +1.91 km, up to 780 m off route), against an overall +2.5 km / +24% gap [F1][RD-1].

That segment is not excused by traffic cause. RD-4(a) needs a traffic-incident fact on the replaced stretch reported before the detour; the trace marks this ✗ and F14 records no incident near the route in the trip window [F3][F14][RD-4]. The only congestion record is CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY speed band 1 during 22:37–22:58 [F11], whose window ends exactly when the off-route segment begins at 22:58 [F3]; a band fact is corroborative only and cannot exempt on its own [F11][RD-4]. Free-flowing AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY and KENT RIDGE ROAD (band 4) [F12][F13] say nothing about the replaced stretch of the optimal route, which is what RD-4 requires; the driver's post-trip account that the expressway "was crawling" [F10] corroborates a cause but not a qualifying exemption [F10][RD-4].

The segment is also not consented to. The complete, fully timestamped chat contains only two messages, both at 22:43 — the rider announcing he is at the kerb outside Mandarin Gallery [F7] and the driver saying he is 5 min away [F8] — well before the 22:49 pickup and the 22:58 segment start [F3][F9][RD-5]. Neither message is a rider agreement to any route, general or named; the driver's post-trip statement [F10] is not consent (G11) [F10][RD-5]. With no rider message before the segment agreeing to it, the finding is counts [F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply: no stop was measured in the segment, and no rider message requested one [F7][F8][RD-3].

Amount: the per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $18.60 ÷ 13.19 km = $1.4102/km [F6][F4]. Refund = unexempted extra_km × rate = 1.91 km × $1.4102/km = $2.6935 → $2.69; the residual ~0.6 km of the billed 2.51 km / $3.54 excess [F1][F4] is corridor drift / map-matching that RD-2 leaves non-refundable, so the full headline gap is not payable [F4][RD-2]. RD-6 does not attach: the driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes, 0 upheld (route 0) [F17], so route_disputes_upheld_90d is not ≥ 1 and profile facts cannot carry the main finding anyway [F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The only rider messages are F7 and F8, both timestamped 22:43, before the pickup at 22:49 and before the segment's 22:58 start [F3][F9]; neither is an agreement to any route change, and the driver's post-trip statement F10 is not rider consent (G11). No rider message before the segment agrees to it, so the segment counts under RD-5 and its extra_km is refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's congestion claim is not a qualifying exemption: RD-4(a) requires a traffic-incident fact on the replaced stretch (the trace marks it ✗ and F14 records no incidents near the route in the trip window), and F11's CEX band 1 window 22:37–22:58 ends when the off-route segment begins at 22:58 [F3][F11][F14][RD-4]; RD-4(b) is corroborative only.

Free-flowing alternatives are irrelevant to the exemption test: F12 and F13 show the roads he used were not jammed, but RD-4 requires evidence targeting the replaced portion of the optimal route, which is missing [F3][F12][F13][F14][RD-4]; RD-1's shortest-and-most-direct duty is not discharged by a longer clear road.

The conditional no_action for F3 fails at its premise: F11 (CEX band 1, 22:37–22:58) does not cover the segment window 22:58–23:05 [F3], F14 records no incident, and no rider consent exists [F7][F8][F9][F10], so the segment is unexempted and RD-2 refund applies rather than no_action [RD-2][RD-4][RD-5].
